title: Finite-valued invariant metrics and a classification of natural groups
summary: Every group $G$, of arbitrary cardinality, admits a right-invariant metric with at most five values whose isometry group is exactly the group $Ξ(G)$ of permutations preserving every inverse-pair difference. Five is sharp. Writing $N(G)$ for the least number of values, including zero, we obtain $N(G)=1$ for the trivial group, $N(G)=2$ for $C_2$ and $C_3$, $N(G)=3$ for every other group outside an explicitly listed set $\mathcal{E}$ of 24 finite groups, $N(G)=4$ on $\mathcal{E}\setminus\{C_2^3, C_3^2\}$, and $N(C_2^3)=N(C_3^2)=5$. The exact result combines Cayley-graph realization theorems…
